samples.summary: Headless copy-paste login is broken while the design doc still promises it. `docs/design/cli.md:176` (unchanged by this diff) still says step 3 "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments", but the happy path now prints `.../auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` WITHOUT `cliState`, and the removed line "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above." is only replaced inside the `catch` of `open()`. On a headless box where `open()` resolves without actually launching a browser (a very common case — `open` shells out to xdg-open/`$BROWSER` and frequently succeeds nominally), the only URL the user can copy is the nonce-less one. Following it makes the backend start a flow with `cliState: undefined`, redirect without `state`, and the listener then rejects with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE telling the user to upgrade the server or pass `--allow-unbound-callback` — advice that is false for an up-to-date server and pushes them to disable the very binding this change adds. Either keep printing the full URL (the doc's contract) or update cli.md step 3 and the headless story to match.
samples.evidence: login.ts:71-87 builds `oauthUrl` with cliState but prints the stripped form unconditionally; full URL printed only in the `catch`. docs/design/cli.md:176 still claims the URL is printed for copy-paste in headless environments.

samples.summary: The new `--allow-unbound-callback` option is not registered in the self-describing schema. cli.md sells `wafflebase schema` as the contract agents read instead of docs ("Self-describing: schema and skill files eliminate documentation lookup", cli.md:1113), and the `login` entry lists only `--server`. The flag is also missing from the Command Tree in cli.md (line 301 shows `login` with no options) even though the prose at cli.md:226 documents it, so the two halves of the same doc disagree.
samples.evidence: registry.ts:43-50 `login` parameters = { '--server': ... } only; docs/design/cli.md:301 `login` line lists no flags.

samples.summary: Scope: the change bundles four separable concerns — (1) OAuth loopback nonce binding across backend+CLI, (2) URL path-segment encoding/rejection hardening (`client/url.ts`), (3) extending `--dry-run` to read and api-key commands, and (4) an unrelated fix to the CI lane-selection test in `scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs`. Concern (4) in particular touches neither the CLI nor auth and has nothing to do with the rest; it makes the change harder to review, revert, and bisect. Splitting the CI-script fix (and arguably the dry-run coverage work) into its own change would fit the repo's per-area design-doc discipline better.
samples.evidence: Diff spans packages/backend/src/auth/*, packages/cli/src/client/url.ts, ~10 command files' dry-run branches, and scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs.

samples.summary: Inconsistent placement of the new dry-run branches relative to the existing try/catch. `docs get` (docs.ts:126), `tabs list` (tabs.ts:15) and `cells get` (cells.ts:21) preview OUTSIDE the surrounding try/catch, so a `seg()` rejection escapes `outputError` and is enveloped only by `runCli`, while the sibling previews in `files get`/`notes get`/`slides get`/`api-keys *` sit inside the try and go through `outputError`. The new tests even encode this divergence (read-dry-run.test.ts asserts one path rejects and another sets exitCode 1). Same command class should produce the same error path/exit-code shape.
samples.evidence: docs.ts:126 (outside try) vs files.ts:113-117 (inside try); packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts comments "`docs get` previews before its try/catch".

samples.summary: The risk table now records an explicitly **Open** vulnerability (nonce readable from the CLI's argv via /proc/<pid>/cmdline) with the remediation sketched (PKCE-shaped `POST /auth/cli/start`) but no tracked follow-up task or doc link. The repo files follow-ups under docs/tasks/; leaving an accepted-open risk with no pointer makes it easy to lose.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. login.ts:71-73 builds oauthUrl including &cliState=<nonce>, but the unconditional stderr line at 74-76 prints the stripped URL without the nonce; the full URL is emitted only inside the catch of open() at 81-87. The design doc contract is unchanged and now contradicted in two places: docs/design/cli.md:175-176 shows step 3 as GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&cliState=<nonce> and states it "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments", and the risk table row at docs/design/cli.md:1177 mitigates "Browser doesn't open (SSH, container)" with "Print the URL so user can copy-paste." The consequence chain is also real: a nonce-less start produces cliState undefined (github-auth.guard.ts:65-76, confirmed by github-auth.guard.spec.ts:92-98), the loopback redirect then omits state (auth.controller.ts:130-131), and login.ts:263-271 fails the login with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE (216-220) advising a server upgrade or --allow-unbound-callback. I considered refuting as already-guarded because the prose at docs/design/cli.md:211-218 was updated to describe the nonce-omitting print, but that update does not reconcile the two remaining contract statements at 176 and 1177, and it does not restore a working copy-paste path when open() resolves without actually launching a browser. Under the design-fit lens this is a major spec/design-doc conformance mismatch, so it stays.
